purpose:
This policy says how {{HOSPITAL_NAME}} meets NABH Hospitals 6th Edition standard IPC.6: The organisation performs surveillance to capture and monitor infection prevention and control data.

It covers objective elements IPC.6.a–i (9 elements).

Chapter intent (official Standards PDF): The organisation implements an effective healthcare associated infection prevention and control programme. The programme is documented and aims at reducing / eliminating infection risks to patients, visitors and providers of care. The programme is implemented across the organisation, including clinical areas and support services. The organisation provides proper facilities and adequate resources to support the infection prevention and control programme. The organisation measures and acts to prevent or reduce the risk of healthcare associated infection in patients and staff. The organisation has an effective antimicrobial management programme through regularly updated antimicrobial policy based on local data and monitors its implementation. Programme also includes monitoring of antimicrobials usage in the organisation. Surveillance activities are incorporated in the infection prevention and control programme. The programme includes disinfection / sterilisation activities and biomedical waste (BMW) management.

This policy owns IPC.6. Related AAC, COP, MOM and PRE duties stay with those policies — cross-reference only. Other IPC standards stay with their own policies.

Words marked «like this» are defaults. A blank marked «________» must be filled before issue.
scope:
This policy applies to staff who deliver clinical care, run support services (housekeeping, laundry, kitchen, CSSD, engineering), handle biomedical waste, or hold occupational-health duties at {{HOSPITAL_NAME}}, including the «Infection Prevention and Control Officer», the Infection Prevention and Control Officer and Nurse, treating doctors, nursing, CSSD, Occupational Health and the Quality Coordinator.

It covers 9 objective elements (IPC.6.a, IPC.6.b, IPC.6.c, IPC.6.d, IPC.6.e, IPC.6.f, IPC.6.g, IPC.6.h, IPC.6.i).

Boundaries: do not copy SHCO equivalent-chapter wording. Do not overwrite HCO AAC, COP, MOM or PRE policies. Spell out abbreviations on first use in training materials. OE counts/levels/asterisks stay with the official portal Standards PDF. Method notes come from the Guidebook Interpretation paragraphs (scanned PDF md5 2c4489ee98de4ae9b49cba168ea9f42a).
policy_statement:
{{HOSPITAL_NAME}} implements IPC.6 so that the organisation performs surveillance to capture and monitor infection prevention and control data.

Staff follow written guidance, keep the records listed in the OE table, and escalate when stop-work triggers fire (if this policy includes a stop-work section).
procedure_steps:
5.1 The scope of surveillance incorporates tracking and analysing of infe...

Surveillance mixes active and passive methods and tracks infection risks, rates and trends for the HAIs and processes the «Infection Prevention and Control Committee» names (at least the HAIs in IPC.5 plus hand hygiene and BMW as applicable).

Denominator rules are written. The «Infection Prevention and Control Nurse» compiles monthly rates for the «Infection Prevention and Control Committee».

Method note (from guidebook interpretation): The organisation shall use a judicious mix of active and passive surveillance. The organisation could lay down the parameters that need to be captured and the process for reporting. The collection of surveillance data is an on-going process and is done at regular intervals (may be monthly and consolidated into an annual report), and the organisation shall take suitable steps based on the analysis. A simple calculation of infected patients (numerator) provides only limited information which would be difficult to interpret. Risk factor analysis would require information for both infected and non-infected patients to calculate infection and risk-adjusted rates.

This is a CORE objective element — non-compliance is not acceptable for accreditation.

5.2 Verification of data is done regularly by the infection prevention an...

The IPC team verifies surveillance data regularly — by reviewing each case or a defined sample — before rates are issued.

The «Infection Prevention and Control Officer» signs the monthly verification. Unverified counts are not used as official rates.

Method note (from guidebook interpretation): The data collected shall be authenticated by the infection prevention and control team by going through every data or by using random sampling. In case the collection of data is done only by the infection prevention and control team, verification is not necessary cc. HM core vF.

5.3 Surveillance is directed towards the identified high-risk activities

Surveillance is directed at the high-risk activities identified in IPC.1.b. Evidence of periodic surveillance in those areas (OT, ICU, dialysis, CSSD, etc.) is on file.

A hospital-wide rate without high-risk-area breakout is not this element.

Method note (from guidebook interpretation): The organisation must be able to provide evidence of conducting periodic surveillance in its identified high-risk activities and high-risk areas. It shall define the frequency and mode of surveillance. The surveillance system shall be appropriate and adhering to national/international guidelines. Surveillance activities include areas where demolition, construction or repairs are undertaken.

5.4 Surveillance includes monitoring compliance with hand-hygiene guidelines

Hand-hygiene compliance is monitored at least «monthly» on an appropriate sample covering all staff categories who touch patients. Results go to the «Infection Prevention and Control Committee» and to the units.

This CORE monitoring is how IPC.3.b is shown to be happening, not a substitute for it.

Method note (from guidebook interpretation): The monitoring shall be done at a minimum once every month. An appropriate sample size shall be chosen and all categories of staff (involved in direct patient care) shall be monitored. The compliance levels shall be shared with the relevant staff. A good tool is the WHO’s “Observation Form”. al BS Sa HB.

This is a CORE objective element — non-compliance is not acceptable for accreditation.

5.5 Surveillance includes mechanisms to capture the occurrence of multi-d...

Surveillance captures occurrence of multi-drug-resistant organisms (for example MRSA, VRE, carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales as microbiology reports them). Infection vs colonisation is distinguished as the «Infection Prevention and Control Committee» defines.

The «Microbiologist» alerts the «Infection Prevention and Control Nurse» of new MDRO isolates the same working day. This Achievement element is evidenced by a working capture mechanism.

Method note (from guidebook interpretation): The organisation shall monitor the occurrence and spread of multi-drug resistant organisms (MDROs) for example methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), multi-drug resistant gram-negative bacteria, Vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) etc.

5.6 Surveillance includes monitoring the effectiveness of housekeeping se...

Effectiveness of housekeeping is monitored on a defined schedule (visual plus, where used, fluorescent marker or ATP as the «Infection Prevention and Control Committee» chooses) in high-risk and public areas.

Results go to housekeeping and the «Infection Prevention and Control Committee». Repeat fails trigger retraining or product/method change. This is CORE.

Method note (from guidebook interpretation): Monitoring of the effectiveness of housekeeping services shall be done regularly. The organisation shall define the periodicity. This is applicable even if the housekeeping services are outsourced. It is mandatory to capture the effectiveness of the housekeeping activities and not just verify if the housekeeping activity has been done as per the defined frequency. To capture effectiveness, the organisation shall identify desired outcome parameters for housekeeping activities. For example, cleanliness of Hospital Premises, Patient feedback on housekeeping services, Staff feedback on housekeeping services The data could be captured using a checklist. This need not mean routine environmental sampling. The swabs and culture plates should not be collected routinely from OT and other high risk areas for monitoring the clean environment. Periodic fumigation is not recommended. Fogging is recommended only in following conditions * Commissioning of new OT * Modification/ renovation of OT * Significant increase in SSI with evidence of evolvement of environment.

This is a CORE objective element — non-compliance is not acceptable for accreditation.

5.7 Feedback regarding surveillance data is provided regularly to the app...

Surveillance feedback — adherence rates, HAI rates, trends and opportunities — is given regularly to the healthcare providers who can act on it (unit in-charges, «Infection Prevention and Control Committee», treating doctors).

A rate that sits only in the IPC office is not feedback. The «Infection Prevention and Control Nurse» keeps the distribution list and dates.

Method note (from guidebook interpretation): The feedback shall include the adherence rates, healthcare associated infection (HAI) rates, trends and opportunities for improvement, including data from other surveillance activities. It could also provide specific inputs to reduce the HAI rate. This could be in the form ofa bulletin/newsletter. I —h.

5.8 The organisation identifies and takes appropriate action to control o...

Outbreaks are defined using baseline rates. Written guidance names who declares an outbreak, isolation/cohorting, communication and when to call the statutory agency.

The «Infection Prevention and Control Officer» leads the response. Delay in declaring when the definition is met is escalated to the «Medical Superintendent».

Method note (from guidebook interpretation): Surveillance shall help early identification of outbreaks. To define as to what constitutes an outbreak, the organisation shall have baseline rates. The organisation implements written guidance for handling such outbreaks.

This objective element is asterisked in the official Standards PDF — documentation of the process is required.

5.9 Surveillance data is analysed and appropriate corrective and preventi...

The «Infection Prevention and Control Committee» analyses surveillance data and assigns corrective and preventive action with owners and due dates. The «Infection Prevention and Control Officer» tracks closure.

Analysis without action is not this element.

Method note (from guidebook interpretation): The Infection Prevention and Control Committee analyses the surveillance data and based on this corrective and preventive actions are taken where necessary. This also includes taking appropriate corrective actions to prevent recurrence after an outbreak, Standard . IPC.7. Infection prevention measures include sterilisation and / or disinfection of instruments, equipment and devices. Objective Elements.
responsibility:
Medical Superintendent
- Accountable that IPC.6 is resourced and followed.
- Acts on outbreaks, sterilisation recalls and exposure events that reach top leadership.

Infection Prevention and Control Officer
- Owns day-to-day implementation and records for this standard.

Infection Prevention and Control Officer
- Coordinates the IPC programme across standards; brings surveillance and incidents to the Infection Prevention and Control Committee.

Infection Prevention and Control Nurse
- Runs day-to-day surveillance, hand-hygiene audit and staff education as this standard requires.

Quality Coordinator
- Audits this policy «quarterly»; holds training acknowledgements.

definitions: The organisation performs surveillance to capture and monitor infection prevention and control data.
exceptions:
1. Do not skip: The scope of surveillance incorporates tracking and analysing of infection risks, rates and trends.
2. Do not skip: Verification of data is done regularly by the infection prevention and control team.
3. Do not skip: Surveillance is directed towards the identified high-risk activities.
4. Do not skip: Surveillance includes monitoring compliance with hand-hygiene guidelines.
5. Do not skip: Surveillance includes mechanisms to capture the occurrence of multi-drug- resistant organisms.
6. Do not skip: Surveillance includes monitoring the effectiveness of housekeeping services.
7. Do not skip: Feedback regarding surveillance data is provided regularly to the appropriate health care provider.
8. Do not skip: The organisation identifies and takes appropriate action to control outbreaks of infections.
9. Do not skip: Surveillance data is analysed and appropriate corrective and preventive actions are taken.
10. Staff who see an IPC.6 rule broken report it the same shift to the «department in-charge» or the «Infection Prevention and Control Officer».
monitoring_audit:
The Quality Coordinator audits this policy «quarterly».

What is monitored each quarter:

- Sample of records for each OE IPC.6.a–i.
- Asterisked elements (h) have document evidence as required.
- CORE elements (adf) show no critical gaps in the sample.
- Stop-work events (if any) are logged with outcome.

This policy is reviewed «annually», and sooner after a related outbreak, sterilisation failure or exposure cluster.
